channel.title: Sayon Pramanik — Writing
channel.description: Research notes, methods and essays on cities, movement, maps, spatial culture and urban research.

item.title: Why processional routes matter to the way we read cities
item.description: Routes are not simply lines between origins and destinations. They are spatial records of memory, negotiation and collective urban life.

item.title: From historical map to spatial data: documenting the difficult middle
item.description: The most consequential decisions in historical GIS often happen between scanning a map and producing a clean analytical layer.

item.title: Capacity is spatial: thinking beyond a single crowd number
item.description: For temporary festival architecture, carrying capacity depends on approach routes, thresholds and flows—not floor area alone.
